_comment: Scoreholio display handles mapped to roster player ids. Derived from the obvious reading of each nickname plus Dave's roster, then VERIFIED against the Friday AM workbook: week 2 comes from the live match log, and workbook total minus week 2 must leave a plausible week 1. All 18 reconciled with zero contradictions, one-to-one, with every two-week player accounted for. Still worth Dave confirming.

duprNames._why: How DUPR spells a player, where that differs from the league files. DUPR is a separate account per person, typed by the player, so spellings drift. Each entry here was confirmed by evidence, not by looking similar.
duprNames._evidence: Scoreholio's Friday AM export (48 games, nicknames) and DUPR's own list for 2026-09-11 (real names) are the same session. Translating both to roster ids matched 28 of 48 until these two entries were added, and 48 of 48 after. A wrong entry cannot raise that number - it would invent a game DUPR does not have - so closing the gap exactly is the confirmation.

_salNote: RESOLVED by Jay 2026-09-12: the two Sal Farruggia rows are one man, the Merrick in a Pickle one. See mergedPlayers. The separate lowercase DUPR account 'Sal farruggia' is still held apart pending confirmation - it was in use over the same months as 'Sal Farruggia' and shares four playing days with it.

mergedPlayers._why: Roster rows Jay has confirmed are the same person. The league files list Sal Farruggia twice, under Merrick in a Pickle and under LI-Kick. Jay says that is one man and he is the Merrick in a Pickle one, so the LI-Kick row folds into it. Every reference to the left id becomes the right id.
mergedPlayers._evidence: Consistent with the Friday AM known-answer test: treating the two rows as one person reproduced all 48 games of that session, exactly as pointing DUPR's Sal at either single row did. The arithmetic could not tell the two explanations apart - Jay could.

_ronnieNote: CONFIRMED by Jay 2026-09-13: Eran Dekel is the man's real name and Ronnie is a nickname he goes by, so 'Ronnie D' on Dave's weekly sheet is him. The site shows the real name. The two names share nothing, so this rested entirely on the week fingerprint (9-13 in 22 games, 202 PF, 212 PA) until Jay confirmed it.
_eagleNote: CONFIRMED by Jay 2026-09-13: BOTH eagle entries are Brett Ritholt - the single eagle on the weekly sheet and the double eagle on the OG Season 9 table. The single one was identified by the week fingerprint (2-9 in 11 games, 94 PF, 122 PA); the double one has no DUPR games at all to fingerprint, so it rested entirely on Jay knowing the club.
_breadyNote: CONFIRMED by Jay 2026-09-13: BReady is Jarred Barretti. Thin name evidence (the B, and BReady reading as a play on Barretti); the week fingerprint (3-8 in 11 games, 93 PF, 109 PA) is what actually identified him.
_crewsSplitNote: NOT YET CONFIRMED. Dave's weekly sheet carries TWO rows, 'Michael Crews' (6-3, 9 games, 87 PF, 80 PA) and 'Michael C.' (2-8, 10 games, 87 PF, 106 PA), neither of which matches any single player. Their sums - 8-11, 19 games, 174 PF, 186 PA - are exactly DUPR's Mike Crews, on all five numbers. The reading is that one man is entered twice on the sheet. Not applied: splitting or merging an identity on arithmetic alone is exactly what this file exists to prevent.
_ambiguousScoreholioNote: OPEN, 2026-09-13. Two Scoreholio handles in the Nov-Dec 2025 exports each match two roster players and neither is resolvable: 'Michael S.' (Michael Scancarello or Michael Spezio, 42 games) and 'Danny M.' (Danny Marino or Danny Miklin, 33 games). One constraint is already proven and must not be lost: 'Scanc' and 'Michael S.' are on OPPOSITE SIDES of three games on 2025-12-04, so they are two different men - if Scanc is Michael Scancarello then Michael S. is Michael Spezio. A 'company' test (matching a handle's team-mates and opponents against each roster player's DUPR partners) was tried and REJECTED: run against the 46 handles resolve.mjs reads with certainty it got 8 of 46 right, so it cannot name anyone. Waiting on Jay or Dave.

sheetHandles._why: Dave's sheets list some players by a handle rather than a name - 'Ronnie D', 'J.Z.', a bare eagle emoji. Each entry maps that handle to the roster id of the real person. Mostly the weekly master sheet, but league tables carry them too.
sheetHandles._method: Dave's sheet covers one week (Sep 6-12) and so does our DUPR match record for those days. Each player's wins/losses/games/points-for/points-against over that window is a five-number fingerprint. Matching fingerprints names the handle.
sheetHandles._control: Run against the 64 players who appear in BOTH sources, the fingerprint identified the right person 64 times out of 64, with no wrong answers and no ties. No two of the 85 players active that week shared a fingerprint. Dave's numbers also agreed with our DUPR-derived records exactly for all 64.
sheetHandles._confirmedBy: Jay, 2026-09-13 - reviewing one at a time the entries where the fingerprint was the ONLY evidence and the name gave no corroboration.

_scoreholioHandleNote: Added 2026-09-13: 'Eddie' -> Edward Rizzi (3 games agree; 'Eddie Rizzi' was already a confirmed handle for him) and 'French Mike' -> Mikel Strauch (11 games agree, and the name corroborates - Mikel is the French spelling of Michael). Between them they were blocking 17 games from carrying a court and a clock.

scoreholioHandles._why: Scoreholio display handles that resolve to players who exist only in the DUPR-widened roster. They cannot live in `confirmed`: that map is checked against Dave's workbook roster, early, before any DUPR-only player exists, and the guard there rightly refuses an unknown id.
scoreholioHandles._how: Identified by known-answer join, not guesswork. The same session exists in BOTH Scoreholio (handles) and DUPR (real names). Resolve the other three players in a game, match on score, and exactly one seat is left - whoever DUPR has sitting in it is the handle.
scoreholioHandles._risk: A wrong entry here cannot corrupt the match list. Enrichment only attaches a court and a clock to a game that already matches on all four players AND the score, so a wrong name simply fails to match and the game stays un-enriched.

_tournamentHandleNote: Handles that Scoreholio's own roster left unnamed for a particular tournament, resolved by Jay from the club's records one night at a time. These are per TOURNAMENT, not per handle, because the same handle is demonstrably different people on different nights - 'Michael S.' is Michael Scancarello on some rosters and Michael Spezio on others, and 'David A.' is Amatulli on 12 rosters and Altman on 3. A global answer would be wrong on one set or the other.

tournamentHandles._confirmedBy: Jay, 2026-09-13, checking the club's own records night by night

_namedByHandNote: Handles Jay named by hand from the unknown-nicknames workbook, checked before they were accepted. The check: if two handles are given the SAME person, do those two handles ever appear in one game? One person cannot be on court twice, so a handle pair that shares a game is a wrong answer, not a synonym. Two answers were refused on that test and are NOT in this map - see _refusedAnswers.

_refusedAnswers._why: Answers that contradict the match log. Kept here so the question is not asked twice and the refusal is not silently forgotten.
_refusedAnswers.Michael S. / Scanc: Both were given as Michael Scancarello, but the two handles play in the SAME GAME 7 times. One of them is someone else - probably Michael Spezio, the other candidate the roster offers.
All three were given as Abigail Fromm. Alison C. and olie K. share a game once, so they are not one person, and none of the three abbreviates to Abigail Fromm. Reads like a dropdown mis-click - Abigail Fromm sits near the top of a 544-name list.

_brettNote: CONFIRMED by Jay 2026-09-14: the three Brett rows are one man, and the correct spelling is the one ending in z - Brett Ritholtz. 'brett ritholt' (219 games), 'Brett' with the eagle emoji (285) and 'Brett Ritholtz' (658) fold into the last of those, 1,162 games in all. EVIDENCE, not just the name: across all 26,477 games no two of the three are ever on court together, which is the same contradiction test that caught the Michael S./Scanc answer. Stronger still, on 2026-04-28 'brett ritholt' plays 9:19-9:59 PM and 'Brett Ritholtz' plays 10:05-11:07 PM in the SAME tournament - consecutive, non-overlapping blocks, which is one person whose handle changed mid-session and not two people in one round robin. 2026-09-01 shows the same shape (9:08-9:19, then 9:38-10:57). The earlier _eagleNote called the eagle handles 'Brett Ritholt'; that was the same man under the spelling without the z, and this merge carries them to the right row.
_duplicatesFoundLiveNote: CONFIRMED 2026-09-14, after the site went live and players started spotting their own names twice. Four more pairs, each one person whose games were recorded under a Scoreholio identity AND a DUPR identity. The test in every case was not the spelling: it was whether the two sets of games are the SAME games - same date, same score, same other three players - with one seat renamed. Vinz Viz -> Vincent Vizcarra (62 of 77 games are twins). Tommy McDonough -> Tom McDonough (all 31 of Tommy's games are twins of Tom's; Tom is the spelling in Dave's Thursday Carpenters workbook). Rudolph -> Rudolf Kormanik (136 twins; 'Rudolph' is a first name only). Peter DeLucia -> Peter DeLucia Jr (all 12 games are twins, on the single night 2026-06-24, so these are NOT a father and son with separate records - the name suggested two people and the games settled it). None of the four pairs ever appears on court together. REJECTED in the same pass: 'tom dero' is NOT either McDonough - zero twin games, and the two date ranges do not even overlap (tom dero May 1 - Jun 12, Tom McDonough Jun 19 - Jul 17).
_feinNote: Jeffrey Fein -> Jeff Fein, confirmed by Jay 2026-09-14. NOTE THE EVIDENCE IS WEAKER HERE than for the other merges in this map, and deliberately recorded as such. The twin-game test that settled Vizcarra, McDonough, Kormanik, DeLucia and the Bretts finds NOTHING here: the two records share no game, no tournament and not one single date. What they show instead is a handover - Jeffrey Fein runs 2025-07-25 to 2025-09-05 (32 games, all Scoreholio) and Jeff Fein begins 2025-10-03 and continues to the present. Consecutive, never concurrent, which is what a renamed account looks like. Supporting: jeff-fein already carried duprNames ['Jeffrey Fein'], so the club's own alias file already said this man is spelled Jeffrey in DUPR; and 19 of Jeffrey Fein's 20 playing contacts are people Jeff Fein has also played (95%, 4th highest of 141 players his size, against a median of 56%). That last figure is suggestive, not proof - three other players score 93-96% without being him. Two different Feins playing in different eras would leave the same trace, so this merge rests on Jay knowing the man, not on the arithmetic. NOT MERGED: 'joseph fein' (18 games, 2024-11-04 to 2024-12-02) is a different first name and, more to the point, a different circle - only 36% of his playing contacts overlap Jeff Fein's, BELOW the 56% median for players his size. The data argues against that one, so it stays separate.
_sweepNote: APPLIED 2026-09-14 from the duplicate sweep (build/dupesweep.mjs), 17 pairs, every one proven by the games rather than by the spelling. A pair qualified only when their records contain the SAME GAME twice - same date, same score, same other three players, one seat renamed - and when the two names have never once been on court together. Counts ran from 348 twin games (Tim/Timothy Lynch) down to 8 (Liam/Liam Hanley); 1,268 double-counted games came out of the totals. DIRECTION: the surviving name is the one Dave's league workbooks use, where either appears in them; otherwise the record with more games. That flipped three from the sweep's default - Michael Crews, Mark Lazo and Chris Price are the workbook spellings and are the ones kept. The full review file, including the 73 pairs left to a human and the 49 the games rule out, is /mnt/user-data/outputs/MIP-duplicate-players.xlsx, regenerated by `npm run dupes`.
_jayPicksNote: Jay's calls from the review workbook, 2026-09-14. Neither pair has a twin game, but both show the same-day consecutive-block signature that settled the Bretts - the two records play back to back on one date, in non-overlapping time blocks, and never once in the same game. David Jackobs -> David Jacobs: on 2024-11-24, Jackobs plays 3:15-5:14 PM and Jacobs plays 5:30-6:54 PM. Jackobs has no games on any other date; Jacobs runs to 2026-09-09 and carries the DUPR spelling. Billy Sc -> Billy Scaduto: on 2026-03-01, Scaduto plays 12:07-1:19 PM and 'Billy Sc' plays 1:27-1:53 PM. 'Billy Sc' is a truncated handle with 4 games on that one date; Scaduto has 1,501 across three leagues.
_displayNamesNote: What a player is CALLED on the site, where the source of a name got it wrong or got only half of it. This renames nothing in the data - it is display only, the id and every game stay exactly as they were, and it is not a merge. It exists because a player's DUPR account is typed by the player, and some of them typed a first name and stopped.

displayNames._why: id -> the name to show. Each one needs a source better than the one it overrides.
displayNames._mike: His DUPR account is typed as the bare word 'Mike', which is where the site was getting it, and with 2,204 games that put a one-word name on the Wall of Fame and near the top of several records. Dave's own weekly sheet calls him Mike Breitinger, and that sheet entry was matched to this player by the five-number week fingerprint and confirmed by Jay on 2026-09-13 - see sheetHandles. The Scoreholio handle 'Mike B.' resolves to him the same way. NOTE 'Mike B.' is genuinely ambiguous in this club - it is also how Michael Bellini appears - so that handle is resolved per tournament from Scoreholio's roster, never globally.

_rosterSourceNote: APPLIED 2026-09-17. The three entries in tournamentHandles marked _source 'Scoreholio Players/Teams roster' were not inferred - they are Scoreholio's own roster for that night, which carries the display name and the real name side by side because Scoreholio must know who a player is to submit to DUPR. That is stronger evidence than any reading of a nickname, and it is why 'Ronnie D' = Eran Dekel and 'Rob S.'/'Robert S.' = Sarraga/Seidner come out right without arithmetic. playerEmail is on that screen and is not collected. Scope is deliberately per-tournament: it names these handles on these nights only, and settles nothing globally.
